name: Clooth-na-Bare

attributes.attribute: W. B. Yeats's transformed Cailleach Bhéirre
not a sovereignty figure in Yeats's handling
seeks a deep lake to drown her fairy life

text: Clooth-na-Bare is a literary figure created by W. B. Yeats. He reshaped the older Cailleach Bhéirre of Irish tradition into this new persona. The change strips away the sovereignty role that the Irish hag carried. Instead Clooth-na-Bare has grown weary of her fairy life. She therefore hunts for the deepest lake of all, seeking water deep enough to drown that life.

okr.objective: Clooth-na-Bare is Yeats's reshaped Cailleach Bhéirre, weary of fairy life and seeking a lake to drown it.
key_results: Yeats built the figure as a changed form of the Irish hag Cailleach Bhéirre.
Unlike her Irish forebear, she carries no sovereignty role.
Weariness drives her search for the deepest lake, where she means to drown her fairy life.
okr.evidence: MacKillop, Dictionary of Celtic Mythology, s.v. Clooth-na-Bare
